newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks surge in active market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks surge in active market.

text.p: Zimbabwe stocks jumped almost two percent on Tuesday on the back of a flow of funds back into the market following the closure last week of an issue by a local merchant bank.

The key industrial index surged 164.57 points -- or 1.6 percent -- to close at 10,408.71 and brokers said they expected the market to continue marching ahead now that the National Merchant Bank (NMB) issue which had tied up most funds was out of the way.

"The market is quite bullish at the moment. Everybody is just trying to place their NMB refunds into the market. Many people are expecting large refunds that's why we are seeing so much activity now than we did in the past two weeks," one broker said.

On the market on Tuesday, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans soared 500 cents to 4,800, merchant banker FMB jumped 200 cents to 4,700, cement producer Porthold rose 50 cents to 1,700 as did blue-chip beverages, supermarkets and hotels conglomerate Delta to 3,150.

Sugar refinery ZSR added 45 cents to 1,425, clothing retailer Edgars climbed 30 cents to 800, sugar producer Hippo added 25 cents to 1,450 while finance house UDC and tobacco company TSL each put on 20 cents to 340 and 680 respectively.
Minings were busier and firmer than of late despite pressure on the bullion price in London on Tuesday.
Gold producer Ashanti leapt 600 cents to 10,600 with brokers saying its big discount to London was drawing investor interest.
Nickel miner Bindura traded 20 cents higher at 800 and Wankie Colliery was 10 cents up at 560.
The mining index rose 16.49 points to 1,020.03.
